items.title: Dead fetcher stub (wellfound.py) and stale comment in main.py mislead contributors
items.description:
### What's wrong

`fetchers/wellfound.py` is a non-functional stub — it builds a request URL, has a `# May need different parsing` comment, and always returns an empty list. It is **not** imported anywhere in `main.py`.

Meanwhile, `main.py` has this comment above the active fetcher imports:

```python
# Remove these broken fetchers:
# lever, workable, recruitee, himalayas, wellfound, remoteok_extended, greenhouse_autodiscovery,
```

This comment is stale and misleading — `lever`, `workable`, and `himalayas` are actually imported and actively used just a few lines above (each marked `# NEW`), while `wellfound` genuinely is unused/broken. A new contributor reading this has no reliable way to tell which fetchers are actually live without cross-checking the import list by hand.

### What to do
1. Remove the unused `fetchers/wellfound.py` stub (or, if the maintainers would rather keep it for future work, move it to a clearly-named location like `fetchers/wip/` so it's obvious it isn't wired in — pick whichever the maintainers confirm they prefer, defaulting to deletion if no response).
2. Update/remove the stale comment block in `main.py` so it accurately reflects which fetchers are currently active vs. unused, and clean up the leftover `# ... rest of build_sections stays the same` comment inside `build_sections()` while you're in there.

### Acceptance criteria
- `fetchers/wellfound.py` is either removed or clearly marked as not-yet-implemented/unused.
- `main.py` no longer contains the misleading "Remove these broken fetchers" comment listing currently-active fetchers as broken.
- `python main.py` still runs successfully (or `main()`'s fetcher loop still works) with no missing-import errors.

### Why this is a good first issue
Pure cleanup — no runtime behavior changes to fetchers that are actually used, but it removes a real source of confusion for the next person trying to understand which parts of the codebase are live.

items.title: Remove committed debug artifacts from fetchers/ and update .gitignore
items.description:
### What's wrong

Two large debug files are checked into git under `fetchers/`:

- `fetchers/debug_yc_page.html` (~119 KB)
- `fetchers/debug_yc_page.png` (~113 KB)

These look like leftover debug output from developing the YC/Playwright fetcher (`fetchers/yc_workatastartup.py`). They aren't referenced by any code and just add ~230 KB of dead weight to the repo. `.gitignore` also doesn't currently cover this kind of debug output, so it's easy for similar files to get committed again by accident.

### What to do
1. Delete `fetchers/debug_yc_page.html` and `fetchers/debug_yc_page.png` from the repo.
2. Add a pattern to `.gitignore` to prevent this from happening again, e.g.:
   ```
   debug_yc_page.*
   ```
   (or a broader `*.html`/`*.png` debug-output pattern if that fits the project's conventions better — use your judgement and explain your choice in the PR).

### Acceptance criteria
- The two files are removed from the repo.
- `.gitignore` is updated so regenerating these debug files locally won't cause them to be re-committed.
- No functional/runtime code changes.

### Why this is a good first issue
Zero application logic involved — just a clean, low-risk repo hygiene fix that's a great way to make a first PR (delete files + edit `.gitignore`).

items.title: TheMuse fetcher only pulls page 0 — missing most jobs
items.description:
### What's wrong

`fetchers/muse.py` hardcodes `"page": 0` when calling the TheMuse API and never loops through subsequent pages:

```python
params = {
    "category": "Technology",
    "location": "Remote",
    "page": 0,
}
r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=15)
```

Because of this, the fetcher silently misses the majority of available listings from TheMuse — it only ever returns whatever fits on the first page of results.

### What to do

Add pagination so the fetcher loops through pages until there are no more results (or a sane max-page cap is hit), similar to how `fetchers/himalayas.py` already does it:

```python
page = 1
max_pages = 20
while page <= max_pages:
    ...
    if not job_list:
        break
    page += 1
```

### Acceptance criteria
- `fetchers/muse.py` fetches all available pages from TheMuse's public API (with a reasonable max-page safety cap).
- Running `python -c "from fetchers import muse; print(len(muse.fetch()))"` returns noticeably more jobs than before.
- No changes needed elsewhere — `main.py` just calls `muse.fetch()` and consumes whatever list comes back.

### Why this is a good first issue
Single file, clear bug, and an existing pagination pattern in the codebase (`fetchers/himalayas.py`) to mirror. No API keys required to test locally.
